headline: Flash Floods Strike Missouri and Iowa as Fire Weather Emergencies Persist Across Wyoming, Montana, and North Dakota
overview: A multi-hazard day unfolds across the United States and globally, with severe flash flooding striking Missouri, Kansas, and Iowa after 4–7 inches of rain, while widespread Red Flag Warnings and High Wind Warnings stretch from Wyoming through North Dakota with gusts to 60 mph. Internationally, Indonesia's karhutla wildfire crisis has scorched more than 202,000 hectares and is sending hazardous transboundary haze across Southeast Asia, while volcanic activity at Kīlauea and Anak Krakatau continues unabated.

events.title: Missouri, Kansas & Iowa Flash Flooding — 4–7 Inches of Rain, Multi-County Warnings
events.location: Northwest Missouri, Northeast Kansas, and Iowa, USA
events.summary: Intense thunderstorms dropped 4–7 inches of rain across northwest Missouri and northeast Kansas overnight into Monday morning, triggering multiple Flash Flood Warnings across Andrew, Holt, Daviess, DeKalb, Gentry, and Harrison counties in Missouri and Doniphan County in Kansas. A broad Flood Watch also covers much of Iowa — including the Des Moines metro and surrounding counties — through Tuesday morning as additional rounds of heavy rainfall are expected. Creeks, streams, urban areas, and highways are flooding, and the NWS Kansas City office described flash flooding as ongoing in several warned areas.

events.title: Wyoming, Montana & North Dakota Fire Weather Emergency — Gusts to 60–75 mph, Humidity Below 10%
events.location: Wyoming, Montana, and North Dakota, USA
events.summary: Critical fire-weather conditions intensified Monday as the NWS issued Red Flag Warnings across central and southwest Wyoming — including Natrona, Fremont, and Sweetwater counties — and a sweeping High Wind Warning for much of western North Dakota, with gusts to 60 mph forecast and humidity dropping as low as 10–15%. In Wyoming's Absaroka Mountains and Upper Wind River Basin, local gusts to 75 mph are possible, while Montana's Snowy and Judith Mountains face 60 mph gusts through 6 PM MDT. Any fires igniting under these conditions are expected to spread rapidly, and outdoor burning is strongly discouraged across all warned areas.

events.title: Indonesia Karhutla Crisis — 202,000+ Hectares Burned, Transboundary Haze Engulfs Southeast Asia
events.summary: Indonesia's annual karhutla (forest and land fire) crisis has reached severe proportions as of September 13–14, with surface and underground peat fires scorching over 202,000 hectares across the archipelago, according to The Nation Thailand. The fires are generating thick transboundary haze that is drifting into neighboring Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand, prompting an environmental coalition to call for recognition of the crisis as ecocide and for transnational corporate accountability. Air quality in affected areas has deteriorated to hazardous levels, with peatland fires — which burn underground and are extremely difficult to extinguish — fueling the most persistent pollution.

events.title: Western Balkans Wildfire Crisis — Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania & Serbia
events.location: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania, Serbia, Western Balkans
events.summary: Wildfires continue to burn across the Western Balkans, with Bosnia and Herzegovina bearing the most severe impact — particularly around the Konjic area — while fires also persist in Montenegro, Albania, and Serbia. EUMETSAT satellite imagery published September 11 captured the breadth of the blazes, which have been driven by high temperatures, low humidity, and strong winds. The crisis has drawn international attention, with Albania reporting destruction of homes in the Himara region and ongoing multi-country firefighting efforts.

events.title: Kīlauea Summit Eruption — Episodic Fountaining and Lava Overflows Continue
events.location: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Big Island, Hawaii, USA
events.summary: Kīlauea's ongoing summit eruption within the Kaluapele caldera continues to produce episodic lava fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter from crater vents, as documented in a USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory monitoring overflight on September 10. The eruption, marked by more than 101 lava overflow events, remains at USGS WATCH alert level. HVO continues 24-hour monitoring as eruptive activity shows no signs of abating.

events.title: Anak Krakatau Eruption — 243+ Events in 2026, Alert Level III Maintained
events.summary: Anak Krakatau remains at Alert Level III (Siaga) and has logged 243 eruptions in 2026 alone, with the volcano continuing to spew lava fountains and ash plumes that have reached 150+ km from the vent; a 25-hour eruption in early September sent ash into Jakarta and Lampung province and was captured in satellite imagery by ESA's Sentinel-5P. AFP fact-checkers confirmed the recent eruption activity is genuine, noting the volcano erupted multiple times in September 2026. Indonesia's Geological Agency has noted the concurrent activity of multiple volcanoes across the archipelago, though they are not considered geologically linked.

events.title: Northern California Red Flag Warnings & PG&E Power Shutoffs — Redding Metro and Sacramento Valley
events.location: Northern California (Sacramento Valley, Shasta, Tehama, Butte, Plumas, Glenn, Colusa Counties), USA
events.summary: The NWS Sacramento office has maintained Red Flag Warnings through 5 PM PDT Monday across the Sacramento Valley and adjacent foothills, including the Redding metro area, citing north-to-northwest winds gusting 20–35 mph and relative humidity as low as single digits. California's Office of Emergency Services has pre-approved firefighting resources for seven counties ahead of the warnings, and PG&E warned of potential public safety power shutoffs across Northern California counties to reduce ignition risk. The conditions are part of a broader multi-day critical fire-weather pattern that has also gripped Nevada, Wyoming, Montana, and the Northern Plains.
